title: Environment variables are stored encrypted and never surface in plaintext
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF and the row where the whole feature's honesty lives.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the ENVIRONMENTS model (environments verify|preview|production x variables), the two operator-only commands, encryption at rest, and the reads that return {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} and NEVER a value. No delivery into spawns, no UI - children 2 and 3.

ARCHITECT DECISION on the question the parent left open ("key derived from the daemon credential, or Windows DPAPI - architect decides"): DERIVE THE KEY FROM THE DAEMON CREDENTIAL. Reasons, so it is not re-litigated: (1) DPAPI is WINDOWS-ONLY and this repo ships on Windows, macOS and Linux - a DPAPI path means either a platform-locked feature or two implementations of the most security-sensitive code in the row; (2) the daemon credential already exists, is already the thing that gates the store, and keeps ONE secret to manage rather than two; (3) it satisfies the stated requirement identically - a store copied WITHOUT the credential is useless - and does so on every platform.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: no per-project or per-environment variable store exists. `grep -rn 'environment\\.set_variable|ENVIRONMENT_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only unrelated hits (agent-spawn-environment.ts's RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS allowlist, a CARRY_FORWARD_ENVIRONMENT_CHANGED fixture). The gap is real.

THE CANARY TEST IS THE POINT, not a nicety. The parent's DoD 2 is a leak hunt: set `MOE_CANARY_<random>`, then grep the STORE FILE BYTES, the event stream, every read response, the wrapper log and every receipt - zero occurrences of the plaintext, while the fingerprint IS present. That test is the only thing standing between this feature and a credential in a bug report, and it must grep BYTES rather than parsed values, because a value can survive in a serialised blob a parsed assertion never looks at.

Parent framing, respected: this is a Stage 2 CAPABILITY and adds no new trust boundary - the store was already sensitive. It is not security-boundary work under the FEATURES ONLY rail; it is a feature that must not leak.
definitionOfDone: `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` published OPERATOR-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test (enumerate the served set from the dispatch seam; verify by deleting each entry from each side and confirming every deletion reds).
Four refusals with a closed code->layer map, each asserted with code AND layer: ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE.

THE CANARY LEAK HUNT (the parent's DoD 2, minus the spawn half which is child 2's): set `MOE_CANARY_<random>`, then grep for the PLAINTEXT in the store file BYTES, the event stream, every read response and every receipt - ZERO occurrences, while the sha256 fingerprint IS present. Grep bytes, not parsed values: a plaintext surviving inside a serialised blob is invisible to a parsed assertion, and that is precisely how this leaks.

ENCRYPTED AT REST, PROVEN ON BYTES: a store copied WITHOUT the daemon credential answers ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE and yields no plaintext when its bytes are grepped. Assert both halves - a refusal alone does not prove the bytes are unreadable.

Reads return {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} and NO value, on every path including refusals - assert that a refusal message never carries the value either, since an error string is the classic leak.
The fingerprint CHANGES when the value changes and is STABLE when it does not - otherwise the operator cannot tell whether an update took effect without seeing the value.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
taskRails: KEY DERIVED FROM THE DAEMON CREDENTIAL, not DPAPI. DPAPI is Windows-only and this repo ships on three platforms; the decision is recorded in the description and is not the worker's to revisit.
A VALUE NEVER LEAVES THE STORE IN PLAINTEXT - not in an event, a receipt, a read, a log or a REFUSAL MESSAGE. The canary greps bytes, not parsed values.
NO DELIVERY AND NO UI: merging variables into verifier/preview/deploy spawns and generating .env.example is child 2; the Environments screen is child 3.
This is a CAPABILITY row under the FEATURES ONLY rail, not trust-boundary work - it introduces no new boundary. Do not expand it into key rotation, audit logging or access control.
NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client: run the generator and quote the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE FINDINGS, MEASURE THE SEAMS, NO EDITS. comment-f26ea546ec794416b4f970cde1c317fc on this row records two things: the scope narrowed (publishing the two commands moved to task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41, so DoD 1 is NOT this row's), and the append-only store means UNSET CANNOT ERASE history. (a) Confirm the gap: `grep -rn 'environment\.set_variable|ENVIRONMENT_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns only unrelated hits (agent-spawn-environment.ts's RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS :14 and PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES :28, a CARRY_FORWARD_ENVIRONMENT_CHANGED fixture). (b) MEASURE THE CRYPTO SEAM: the daemon uses `node:crypto` widely but ONLY `createHash` (activation-ledger-codec.ts:16, activation-receipts-measure.ts:10 and others) — there is NO existing encryption helper, so the cipher is new. Choose an AEAD (AES-256-GCM is the obvious one), and record the choice, the nonce discipline and where the salt lives. (c) Read `identity/session-authenticator.ts:68`, which documents why credential comparison is constant-time and how an early length check leaks length through timing — the same care applies here. (d) Confirm the store takes opaque `Uint8Array` payloads (store-contracts.ts:32,43) so sealed bytes need no schema fight.
implementationPlan.note:
MEASURED, NO EDITS.

(a) GAP CONFIRMED. `grep -rnE 'environment\.set_variable|ENVIRONMENT_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` -> zero hits for any variable store. Only unrelated: agent-spawn-environment.ts:14 RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS, :28 PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES, verifier-process-runner.ts:31, projects/project-launch-environment.ts (stack keys), PROJECT_MANAGER_LAUNCH_ENVIRONMENT_INVALID, control-room CARRY_FORWARD_ENVIRONMENT_CHANGED fixture, packages/context dead-end-journal ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER. `ls apps/daemon/src/environment` -> "No such file or directory". Gap is real.

(b) CRYPTO SEAM. `grep -rnE 'createCipheriv|createDecipheriv|scrypt|pbkdf2|hkdf' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` -> ZERO hits repo-wide. Only randomBytes (moe-init.ts:232, goal-catalog-read.ts:131, pairing entropy) and createHmac (goal-catalog-cursor.test.ts). Confirms the architect's finding: NO encryption helper exists; the cipher is genuinely new.
CHOICE RECORDED: AES-256-GCM (AEAD, in node:crypto, authenticated so a wrong key FAILS rather than returning garbage).
KEY DERIVATION: HKDF-SHA256 over the daemon credential, NOT scrypt/pbkdf2. The credential is already high-entropy - `moe-init.ts:152` mints it as `randomHex(CREDENTIAL_BYTES)` - so this is key-derivation from a secret, not password-stretching; a work factor would buy nothing and cost ~100ms per seal.
SALT: 16 random bytes generated PER SEAL and stored in the sealed blob header. No ambient salt file to lose, and it keeps the blob self-describing.
NONCE: 12 random bytes PER SEAL, stored in the blob. Never fixed, never derived from a counter.
BLOB LAYOUT: [version:1][salt:16][nonce:12][tag:16][ciphertext:n].

(c) TIMING CARE. Read identity/session-authenticator.ts:60-73: `credentialSha256Of` + `constantTimeEquals` digest-then-compare because `timingSafeEqual` demands equal lengths and an early length check leaks credential LENGTH through timing. Applies here: no length-dependent branch on the credential. GCM tag verification is already constant-time inside node's `decipher.final()`, which throws on mismatch - I catch and convert to a fail-closed result rather than comparing tags by hand.

(d) STORE TAKES OPAQUE BYTES - CONFIRMED. store-contracts.ts:32 `EventDraft.payload: Uint8Array`, :43 `CommitInput.commandBytes: Uint8Array`, :76 `committedResultBytes`. Store API measured: `SqliteEventStore.commit(CommitInput)` (sqlite-event-store.ts:259), `readEvents(aggregateId)` (:355), `getAggregateVersion` (:295), `openForProject(path, projectId)` (:109, FILE-backed, durability "WAL_FILE"), `openEphemeralForProjectTest` (:131, in-memory).
LEAK VECTOR FOUND AND AVOIDED: `commitExpectedVersionDecision` persists `committedResultBytes` AND `requestBytes` as durable bytes (session-ledger.ts:142-152 JSON-stringifies both). Anything a value touches there is durable plaintext. This row will use plain `store.commit()` and will keep the value out of `commandBytes` entirely - only the SEALED blob ever reaches durable bytes. The canary in step 5 greps the file bytes precisely to prove this.
WAL NOTE for step 5/6: a file-backed store is WAL_FILE durability, so bytes can sit in `<db>-wal` / `<db>-shm`, not only `<db>`. The canary must close the store first and then grep EVERY `store.db*` file, not just the .db - grepping only the .db would be a false green.

(e) CONTRACT SHAPE to mirror, read in full: planning/expansion-request-contracts.ts:49-101 - closed `*_CODE_LAYERS` object `satisfies Readonly<Record<string, Layer>>`, code roster DERIVED as `Object.keys(...).sort()`, `expansionRequestRefusal(code)` takes NO layer argument so code and layer cannot disagree (:150-162). Also identity/session-credential-digest.ts:56-64: refusal `detail` is FIXED PROSE, never interpolated - "an interpolated detail is how a digest ... escapes through the one field a refusal is allowed to carry". Both patterns adopted; the second is directly DoD 5.

(f) BRIDGE CONVENTION measured: `cat apps/daemon/src/planning/expansion-request-contracts.js` -> `export * from "./expansion-request-contracts.ts";` - one line, no build step.

(g) DEPENDENCY EDGE: apps/daemon/package.json declares `"@moe/store": "workspace:*"`; daemon modules already import from the bare specifier `@moe/store` and typecheck. No manifest edit needed.

(h) COMMENT-f26ea546 READ. Scope narrowed: DoD 1 (publishing the two commands on the roster) is task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41's, NOT this row's - I will touch none of daemon-command-vocabulary.ts / -registry.ts / -families.ts / mcp-tool-allowlist.ts / the generated client (step 7b proves the absence). implementationPlan.description: THE CIPHER, in a new apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-cipher.ts (+ its `.js` bridge). Derive the key FROM THE DAEMON CREDENTIAL — the decision is recorded in this row's description and is not the worker's to revisit (DPAPI is Windows-only and this repo ships on three platforms). Expose seal/open over bytes, with the key derivation INJECTABLE so tests can drive a known key without a real credential on disk. NONCE DISCIPLINE IS THE PART TO GET RIGHT: a repeated nonce under the same key breaks AES-GCM catastrophically, so generate per-seal and store it with the ciphertext; state in a comment why. `open` with the WRONG key must FAIL AUTHENTICATION rather than return garbage — that is the property that makes a copied store useless rather than merely scrambled. Test: round trip; wrong key fails closed; a tampered ciphertext fails closed; two seals of the SAME plaintext produce DIFFERENT bytes (proving the nonce is not fixed — a test that only round-trips passes with a constant nonce).
implementationPlan.note:
THE CIPHER LANDED. AES-256-GCM, key derived from the daemon credential via HKDF-SHA256.

TDD ORDER OBSERVED. Test written first; RED confirmed before any production byte existed:
  `Error: Cannot find module './environment-cipher.js' imported from .../environment-cipher.test.ts` / `Test Files 1 failed (1)` / `Tests  no tests`.
Then GREEN:
  `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/environment/environment-cipher.test.ts`
  -> `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  15 passed (15)`.
(Executed-test evidence per global rail 8: the count line reads 15, not 0.)

BLOB LAYOUT, fixed width so framing is decided before a key is touched:
  [version:1][salt:16][nonce:12][tag:16][ciphertext:n]
`ENVIRONMENT_SEAL_HEADER_BYTES` = 45, derived from the four size constants rather than restated.

THE DECISIONS, so they are not re-litigated:
- KEY FROM THE DAEMON CREDENTIAL, not DPAPI - per the row description and task rail 1. Recorded in the module header with the reasons (DPAPI is Windows-only; this ships on three platforms; the credential already gates the store).
- HKDF-SHA256, NOT scrypt/PBKDF2. The credential is machine-minted high-entropy hex (`cli/moe-init.ts:152` `randomHex(CREDENTIAL_BYTES)`), not a human password. A work factor defends against GUESSING a low-entropy secret; there is nothing to guess here, so scrypt would buy zero security and cost ~100ms per seal AND per open. Reasoning is in the header so a later reader does not "harden" it into a slowdown.
- HKDF `info` = "moe/environment-variable-seal/1" for domain separation: this derivation can never collide with another use of the same credential.
- PER-SEAL random salt AND per-seal random nonce, both stored in the blob. The per-seal salt means every value gets its own derived key, so the nonce space is not even shared between two values.

NONCE DISCIPLINE - why the header spells it out. A repeated (key, nonce) pair under AES-GCM is not a degradation, it is a total break: two ciphertexts under one nonce leak their XOR AND the GHASH authentication subkey becomes recoverable, so an attacker can forge blobs the daemon accepts. A hard-coded nonce passes every round-trip test ever written. Hence the dedicated arm, and it is deliberately stronger than "the two blobs differ": it asserts the SALT SLICE differs AND the NONCE SLICE differs, then re-opens both. Pinning either field alone still repeats a (key, nonce) pair, so a one-sided assertion would have been vacuous against half the mistake.

FAIL-CLOSED `open`, proven on four tamper sites, not one. `it.each` flips one bit at the ciphertext, tag, nonce and salt offsets - all four must answer AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Plus: wrong credential, EMPTY credential, and a SALT SPLICED from a different seal of the same credential (that last one proves the salt genuinely participates in the derivation - a salt that were ignored would let the splice open).

MALFORMED vs AUTHENTICATION_FAILED kept distinct: truncated blob and unknown version byte answer MALFORMED (framing, decided before a key is touched); everything else answers AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Distinguishing them tells a caller "corrupt record" from "wrong key" without either answer revealing anything about the value.

LEAK GUARDS ALREADY IN THIS LAYER (DoD 5's first half, at the cipher seam):
- the sealed bytes are asserted NOT to contain the plaintext marker (`Buffer.includes`, byte-level, not a parsed check);
- the failure result is asserted to have EXACTLY the keys `["ok","reason"]` - so a plaintext or credential cannot be smuggled in a field nobody thought to name;
- `JSON.stringify(failure)` is asserted to contain neither the plaintext marker nor EITHER credential. Node's cipher error text is swallowed by design (comment says why): relaying it would put cipher internals into whatever log the refusal reaches.

TIMING: no length-dependent branch on the credential, following `identity/session-authenticator.ts:66-73`. HKDF consumes the credential whole; the empty-credential case takes the SAME path rather than an early exit. Tag comparison happens inside node's constant-time GCM verification, never by hand.

EMPTY VALUE round-trips (0-byte plaintext) - a legal variable value that a naive length guard would have rejected.

SIZE: environment-cipher.ts 154 lines (cap 250). Bridge `environment-cipher.js` is the one-line `export * from "./environment-cipher.ts";` matching the measured convention.

Drills for these arms are step 7's, per the plan.

implementationPlan.description: THE CONTRACT MODULE, in a new apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-contracts.ts (+ `.js` bridge). Export the environments roster (verify | preview | production), the variable-name validity rule, the size bound, and a CLOSED code->layer map for ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN and ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE, with the code roster DERIVED from the map's keys — mirroring planning/expansion-request-contracts.ts, whose header explains why the refusal factory takes no layer argument. Also export the READ shape: `{name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt}` and NOTHING ELSE. Making the read shape a typed contract here is what stops a value being added to it later by accident.
implementationPlan.note:
THE CONTRACT MODULE LANDED.

TDD: RED first (`Cannot find module './environment-contracts.js'`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests no tests`), then GREEN:
  `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/environment/environment-contracts.test.ts`
  -> `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  35 passed (35)`.

WHAT IT DECLARES:
- `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES` = ["preview","production","verify"] (sorted, frozen), `isEnvironmentName` refuses case variants ("Production", "PRODUCTION"), "staging", "", trailing space, and non-strings.
- `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_NAME_PATTERN` = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/u with `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` 128. Deliberately narrower than a shell tolerates BECAUSE these names are destined for a spawned process's environment block (child 2's delivery), and a name carrying `=`, a NUL or a newline is how an environment block gets split into something else. Refusal arms cover exactly those: empty, lowercase, leading underscore, leading digit, hyphen, dot, space, equals, NUL, newline, non-strings, plus at-bound (128 accepted) and one-past-bound (129 refused).
- `MAX_ENVIRONMENT_VALUE_BYTES` = 4096, bounded in UTF-8 BYTES not code units. Pinned by an arm that fills the bound with 4-byte astral code points: `"\u{1F600}".repeat(1024)` accepted, one more refused. A code-unit bound would have let that value reach 4x the intended size, and the arm reddens if anyone "simplifies" to `value.length`.

THE CLOSED MAP, four codes, layer derived:
  ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN -> SCOPE, ENV_NAME_INVALID -> NAME, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE -> KEY, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE -> VALUE.
`ENVIRONMENT_CODES` is DERIVED as `Object.keys(ENVIRONMENT_CODE_LAYERS).sort()`, and an arm asserts the derivation holds rather than only asserting the literal list - so the two cannot drift. Layer coverage is asserted BIDIRECTIONALLY (global rail 9's shape): every layer used by a code is rostered AND every rostered layer is used by some code, by set-equality, so a rostered-but-dead layer reds just as a used-but-unrostered one does.
`environmentRefusal(code)` takes NO layer argument - the layer and the detail are looked up - so a call site cannot mint a code/layer pair that disagrees. Mirrors expansion-request-contracts.ts:150-162.

WHY ONE CODE FOR THREE KEY FAILURES, recorded in the module: absent credential, unreadable credential and a credential that is present but WRONG all answer ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE. Splitting them would let a caller probe whether a credential is merely missing or actually incorrect - a fact about the secret.

DoD 5's structural half is enforced HERE, not only asserted downstream:
- `ENVIRONMENT_REFUSAL_DETAILS` is a frozen constant keyed by code, `satisfies Readonly<Record<EnvironmentCode,string>>`, so a code without a detail fails to compile. An arm asserts the detail key set EQUALS the code roster.
- An arm asserts NO detail contains a digit and none contains "${". That is deliberately stricter than it needs to be today: it stops the habit of interpolating ("must be under 4096 bytes"), which is the on-ramp to interpolating the value itself. Same rule and same reason as identity/session-credential-digest.ts:56-64.
- `environmentRefusal` returns a FROZEN record with exactly ["code","detail","layer","ok"] - asserted by sorted-key equality, so a fifth member cannot be added quietly.

THE READ SHAPE is a typed contract with a rostered key set: `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_READ_KEYS` = ["fingerprintSha256","isSet","name","updatedAt"], asserted by exact array equality. Plus a second arm that asserts no rostered key name contains "value", "secret" or "plaintext" - a cheap tripwire against the exact mistake this row exists to prevent. `EnvironmentVariableRead.isSet` is typed `true`, not `boolean`: an absent variable is ABSENT from the read, never present-with-isSet-false, so there is no shape that could carry a stale fingerprint for something unset.

`environmentValueFingerprint` is sha256 of the PLAINTEXT's UTF-8 bytes, hex. Header records why not the ciphertext: seals are salted per write, so a ciphertext fingerprint would change on every write and tell the operator nothing about whether their update changed the value. Pinned against FIXED VECTORS (sha256("") = e3b0c442... and sha256("abc") = ba7816bf...) rather than self-agreement, so swapping the digest algorithm reds instead of quietly passing. Also asserted CHANGES-on-change / STABLE-on-same (DoD 6's contract half; the store-level half is step 4).

SIZE: environment-contracts.ts 154 lines (cap 250). Bridge is the one-line `export *`.

implementationPlan.description: THE STORE, in a new apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts (+ `.js` bridge), writing sealed bytes as an event payload and folding the current state per environment. Reads return the contract shape from step 3 — name, isSet, fingerprint, updatedAt — and NEVER a value, on EVERY path including refusals. The fingerprint is the sha256 of the PLAINTEXT (it is the operator's only feedback that an update took, since they can never see the value back) and must CHANGE when the value changes and be STABLE when it does not. `unset` removes the variable from the CURRENT state. Test over a real store: set/read/unset round trip; fingerprint changes on update and is stable on a no-op re-set; ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENV_NAME_INVALID and ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE each assert code + layer; ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE when the key cannot be derived.
implementationPlan.note:
THE STORE LANDED, driven over a REAL SqliteEventStore on every arm - no fakes.

TDD: RED first (`Cannot find module './environment-store.js'`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests no tests`), then GREEN.
GATES THIS STEP:
  `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/environment/` -> `Test Files  4 passed (4)` / `Tests  98 passed (98)`
  `npx tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> `TSC-EXIT:0`, empty log (exit captured directly, NOT through a pipe - a piped run reports tail's status).

FILE SPLIT, because environment-store.ts first measured 271 lines against the 250 target. Split by responsibility, not by line count:
- environment-fold.ts (91) - decodes bytes THIS SLICE WROTE, folds to current state. Never sees a credential, cannot open anything, so no decode path here can leak a value.
- environment-projection.ts (155) - resolves the key, opens every seal, projects the read shape, and holds `admitEnvironment`.
- environment-store.ts (152) - the three entry points and the commit.
All production files now <=155 lines.

WHAT REACHES DURABLE BYTES (the design decision that makes step 5 provable):
- event payload: sealed blob (base64), plaintext fingerprint, name, environment, updatedAt.
- commandBytes: SUBJECT ONLY - {environment, kind, name}. NO value.
This is deliberate and commented. `commitExpectedVersionDecision` (the path session-ledger.ts uses) persists `committedResultBytes` AND `requestBytes` as durable bytes; a value routed through either would be durable plaintext. This slice uses plain `store.commit()` and keeps the value out of every field except the seal.

READS OPEN THE SEAL AND DISCARD THE PLAINTEXT - and this is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces. If a read answered straight from the fold: (1) `isSet` would mean "bytes are on disk" rather than "the daemon can recover this value"; (2) A STORE COPIED WITHOUT THE CREDENTIAL WOULD HAPPILY LIST ITS VARIABLES, and DoD 4 would be false. Opening on read is what makes the copy useless rather than merely undelivered. Pinned by the "credential present but WRONG" arm.

THE RETURNED FINGERPRINT IS DERIVED FROM THE OPENED PLAINTEXT, not read back from the payload. The payload's copy is durable EVIDENCE (and DoD 3 requires it be present in the bytes), but it is NOT covered by the GCM tag, so a tampered payload could carry any fingerprint. The answer is computed from the plaintext GCM actually authenticated. Stored copy = evidence; derived copy = answer.

A WRITE VALIDATES THE KEY BEFORE IT COMMITS. Sealing succeeds under ANY non-empty credential, so a write under the wrong credential would otherwise land bytes nobody can ever open and only fail afterwards. `admitEnvironment` opens the whole existing state first. Pinned by "commits NOTHING when a write arrives under the WRONG credential", which reads back UNDER THE RIGHT CREDENTIAL and asserts only the original name survives - an arm that would stay green under a naive `expect(result.ok).toBe(false)`.

REFUSAL ORDER IS FIXED AND ASSERTED: scope -> name -> size -> key. Each code is minted by exactly one surface, so a doubly-invalid call has ONE stable answer. Arm: {environment:"staging", name:"bad-name"} answers ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN/SCOPE, not whichever check happened to run first.

ALL FOUR REFUSALS ASSERT CODE **AND** LAYER (global rail 1), on set, unset and read where each applies:
- ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN/SCOPE x5 inputs ("staging","Production","PRODUCTION","","prod") x3 entry points.
- ENV_NAME_INVALID/NAME x5 shapes (lowercase, leading digit, hyphen, equals, empty) x set+unset.
- ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE/VALUE at bound+1, AND a separate arm proving the bound is UTF-8 BYTES: 1025 astral code points whose `.length` is well under 4096 still refuses. A code-unit bound would pass the first arm and fail this one.
- ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE/KEY x4 causes: absent credential (null), EMPTY credential (""), a source that THROWS (the EACCES-shaped case), and a credential present but WRONG.
EMPTY == ABSENT is not arbitrary: `daemon-main.ts:166` reads `env["MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL"] ?? ""`, so "" is exactly what an unset credential looks like in production.

DoD 6 (fingerprint) OVER THE REAL STORE: CHANGES on update; STABLE across a no-op re-set of the same value even though the SEAL BYTES DIFFER (per-seal salt+nonce) - which is the arm that proves the fingerprint is over plaintext, not ciphertext; and a third arm proving a SIBLING variable's fingerprint stays stable while another is updated twice.

DoD 5 (no value on any path) at the store seam: three refusal arms JSON.stringify the whole refusal and assert the submitted secret is absent - including the oversized-value case, where the value is the thing being complained about. A fourth asserts neither credential appears.

ALSO COVERED: environments stay separate (verify/preview/production); listing is name-sorted regardless of write order; an EMPTY value is SET and distinct from absent; unset is IDEMPOTENT on an absent name; a name can be re-set after unset with a

THE EXFILTRATION IS REAL, not simulated. `exfiltrate()` writes a random `MOE_CANARY_<32 hex>` through the PRODUCTION write path, then CLOSES the store, then `copyFileSync`s the database file. The close is load-bearing: SQLite is in WAL mode, so without checkpointing, the copied `.db` could be missing the record entirely and every assertion below would be about an empty file. That is exactly the false green this arm exists to avoid.

BOTH HALVES ASSERTED, per the DoD - and the second is the one that matters, because an attacker holding the file does not run the daemon:
HALF 1, THE DAEMON REFUSES. ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE + KEY layer on FOUR causes against the copy: no credential (null), EMPTY credential (""), credential PRESENT BUT UNREADABLE (a source that throws EACCES), credential present but WRONG.
HALF 2, THE BYTES ARE UNREADABLE. `readFileSync(copyPath)` searched for the plaintext -> absent; searched for a 16-byte PREFIX WINDOW -> absent (a leak that stored only part of a value is still a leak); and the FINGERPRINT is asserted PRESENT, so "no plaintext" cannot be satisfied by an empty or truncated copy.
HALF 2b, THE CIPHER DIRECTLY. The sealed blob is pulled OUT of the copied file through the production fold and fed to `openEnvironmentValue` - what an attacker with a hex editor and this source would do. Wrong credential -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Empty credential -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. And the blob itself is searched for the plaintext -> absent, with its length asserted to be exactly ENVIRONMENT_SEAL_HEADER_BYTES + the value's UTF-8 length (imported constant, not a literal 45), so a blob that had quietly stopped being ciphertext would red on size.

THE CONTROLS THAT KEEP IT HONEST - without these the whole file could pass on a corrupt copy:
- "is INTACT": the copy is read with the RIGHT credential and yields the variable with the expected fingerprint. So a refusal in the other arms means "unreadable without the key", not "unreadable, full stop".
- "OPEN under the right credential": the sealed bytes taken from the copy DO open and decode BACK TO THE EXACT SECRET. This is the strongest single statement in the file - the ciphertext in the exfiltrated copy is sound and complete, and the only thing standing between it and the plaintext is the daemon credential.

THE UNREADABLE-CREDENTIAL ARM ALSO CHECKS WHAT THE REFUSAL DID NOT SAY. The thrown error is `EACCES: permission denied, open '.moe/credential'`. The refusal is asserted to contain neither "EACCES" nor ".moe/credential" nor the secret. A refusal that relayed the exception would publish where the credential lives - and node error messages are exactly the channel through which an interpolated detail leaks.

TWO PLANNING FINDINGS before this row is worked (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05).

1. SCOPE NARROWED. Publishing `environment.set_variable` / `environment.unset_variable` on the roster and fencing them MCP-excluded moved to task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41 - this row's roster measured ~12 distinct files against the 10-file hard cap. This row owns the CIPHER, the CONTRACT and the ENCRYPTED STORE. DoD 1 (the published commands) is therefore that sibling's, not this row's; DoD 2-6 stay here, minus the spawn half of the canary which is task-72b22fcf's.

2. UNSET CANNOT ERASE, AND THE ROW SHOULD SAY SO. The store is an APPEND-ONLY event log - `packages/store/src/store-contracts.ts` persists `payload: Uint8Array` per event and events are never mutated in place; the whole system replays from them. So an `environment.unset_variable` removes a variable from the CURRENT state, but the ciphertext of every value ever set REMAINS IN HISTORY. That is not a defect to fix here - it is a property to state, because two reasonable people will otherwise assume opposite things:
   - What unset DOES guarantee: the value is no longer current, no longer delivered to any spawn, no longer readable through the reads.
   - What it does NOT: erase the ciphertext from the event stream, or make a previously-exported store safe if the key later leaks.
   The key is derived from the daemon credential (the decision recorded in this row's description), so the history is unreadable without it - which is what makes this acceptable rather than alarming. But an operator who pastes a production secret, realises the mistake, and unsets it has NOT scrubbed their store, and the runbook should say that plainly. Key rotation would be the real remedy and is explicitly out of scope under the FEATURES ONLY rail.

I am adding a DoD clause for it rather than leaving it implicit: the row must ASSERT that a value survives in the event stream as ciphertext after unset (so nobody later mistakes unset for erasure), and must state the limitation in whatever doc the parent's runbook clause covers. Asserting it also protects the canary: a test that greps the event stream for the PLAINTEXT after an unset must still find zero, which is the property that actually matters.

MEASURED SEAMS for the worker: the daemon already uses `node:crypto` widely but only `createHash` (activation-ledger-codec.ts:16, activation-receipts-measure.ts:10, and others) - there is no existing encryption helper, so the cipher module is new. `identity/session-authenticator.ts:68` shows the codebase already reasons about timing leaks on credential comparison; follow that care. The store takes opaque `Uint8Array` payloads, so sealed bytes fit an event payload without a schema fight.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, Windows DPAPI for the at-rest key: the parent left it to the architect and DPAPI is Windows-only while this repo ships on Windows, macOS and Linux — it would mean a platform-locked feature or two implementations of the most sensitive code in the row. The daemon credential already exists, already gates the store, keeps ONE secret to manage, and makes a copied store useless on every platform. REJECTED, keeping the roster publication in this row: it measured ~12 distinct files against the 10-file hard cap, so the two commands moved to task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41 along the interface axis. REJECTED, a round-trip-only cipher test: it passes with a constant nonce, which breaks AES-GCM catastrophically — hence the 'two seals of the same plaintext differ' arm and its drill. REJECTED, asserting the canary on parsed values: a plaintext surviving inside a serialised blob is invisible to a parsed assertion, which is precisely how this class of feature leaks; the greps are over bytes. REJECTED, treating unset as erasure: the store is append-only, so the honest position is that unset makes a value non-current and unreadable-without-the-key, and the row asserts that rather than implying a scrub.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. THE GAP IS REAL: no per-project or per-environment variable store exists; the only `ENVIRONMENT_` hits are agent-spawn-environment.ts's closed allowlist constants (`RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` :14, `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES` :28) and a CARRY_FORWARD fixture. THERE IS NO ENCRYPTION HELPER ANYWHERE: the daemon imports `node:crypto` in many places but only `createHash` (activation-ledger-codec.ts:16, activation-ledger-contracts.ts:22, foundation-activation-transition.ts:20, activation-receipts-measure.ts:10, activation-receipts-ports.ts:9), so the cipher module is genuinely new rather than an extension. THE STORE TAKES OPAQUE BYTES: store-contracts.ts persists `payload: Uint8Array` (:32, :43) and `committedResultBytes` (:76), so sealed bytes fit an event payload without a schema change — and, because the log is APPEND-ONLY and replayed, a sealed value stays in history after unset, which is the finding recorded in comment-f26ea546. PRIOR ART FOR THE CARE REQUIRED: identity/session-authenticator.ts:68 documents constant-time credential comparison and why an early length check leaks length through timing. THE CONTRACT SHAPE to mirror is planning/expansion-request-contracts.ts (closed code->layer map, derived code roster, layer-less refusal factory).
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — a plaintext secret somewhere durable. The canary greps BYTES rather than parsed values because a value surviving inside a serialised blob is invisible to a parsed assertion, and the drill in step 7 forces a refusal message to carry the value so the arm proves it bites. SECOND — nonce reuse. A fixed nonce passes every round-trip test and breaks AES-GCM completely; the 'two seals differ' arm plus its drill is the only thing that catches it, and it is the single most likely cryptographic mistake here. THIRD — `open` returning garbage instead of failing authentication on a wrong key: that would make a copied store scrambled rather than useless, which is a materially weaker claim than the one the row makes. FOURTH — mistaking unset for erasure: the log is append-only, and an operator who pastes a production secret and unsets it has NOT scrubbed their store; the row asserts the ciphertext persists so nobody later assumes otherwise, and the limitation belongs in the runbook. FIFTH — scope leak into the sibling's roster files, which would both breach the cap and collide; step 7(b) makes their absence a proof obligation. SIXTH — drill restores on UNTRACKED modules need out-of-tree SHA256 comparison in a separate call (global rail 13).
